entities.summary: Sundiata Keita was a prince and founder of the Mali Empire. He was also the great-uncle of the Malian ruler Mansa Musa, who is regarded as the wealthiest person of all time, although there are no reliable ways to accurately calculate his wealth.

entities.name: Sunjata Keïta
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sunjata Keïta (c. 1215–1255) stands as the legendary founder of the Mali Empire, a monumental West African polity that dominated the region for centuries. Emerging from the Mandinka heartland in the early 13th century, Keïta unified disparate chiefdoms and established a robust administrative and military structure that laid the groundwork for one of history's wealthiest and most culturally influential empires. His reign marked a pivotal transition from fragmented local polities to a cohesive, expansive state, fundamentally reshaping the political and economic landscape of Medieval West Africa.

The ascent of Sunjata Keïta culminated in the decisive Battle of Kirina around 1235 CE, where his forces triumphed over Soumaoro Kanté, the powerful sorcerer-king of the Sosso. Following this victory, Keïta consolidated his authority, establishing Niani as the capital and presiding over the promulgation of the Manden Charter (Kouroukan Fouga), an oral constitution outlining rights, responsibilities, and social organization for the newly formed empire. His military campaigns extended Malian control over strategic gold-producing regions and vital trade routes, integrating diverse ethnic groups under a common political framework.

Keïta's organizational genius and military prowess created an enduring state that profoundly influenced subsequent West African history. The Mali Empire, built on his foundations, facilitated the flourishing of trans-Saharan trade, the spread of Islam, and the development of major intellectual and commercial centers like Timbuktu and Djenné. His legacy directly enabled the golden age of the empire under his great-nephew, Mansa Musa, whose legendary pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324 showcased Mali's immense wealth and power to the wider world.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sunjata Keïta's unification of disparate Mandinka chiefdoms into the Mali Empire profoundly shaped the political, economic, and cultural trajectory of West Africa for centuries, directly enabling the region's golden age under his successors and influencing the course of trans-Saharan trade.
